Give it something to finish.

See what happens when you press Tab in Bash, fish, and zsh, with and without COMPLETE-ME.

See the completion guide for shell examples.

Where ordinary Tab runs out of answers

A script you just wrote

Shells can complete filenames right away. Completing a new command’s flags often takes a definition for that program. COMPLETE-ME can learn the grammar from help, man pages, or supported script source. The Python recording shows it completing --format on the first Tab.

A value that changes

For supported tools, Tab can look at the selected runtime. Pick a tmux window that’s open now, a Docker container with its status, or a Proxmox backup on the selected node. Existing shell completions still handle the commands they already know.

A line worth keeping

Complete in the middle of an SSH command and keep the host at the end. Press Alt+J when you need a snippet, or type 2*(34+sqrt(81))= and press Tab to fill in the answer. Use ans in the next calculation.

Try it in your shell
